seed_references.verdict: Authoritative, well-structured preservation guidance confirming that emulation preserves interactive behavior but faces severe legal and system-imaging barriers, and that format obsolescence is often less critical than institutional obsolescence.

Peer-reviewed empirical benchmark (full text also opened on DHQ at https://digitalhumanities.org/dhq/vol/13/1/000411/000411.html) proving that human appraisal and lifecycle management—not static storage—drive preservation cost, and that tiered decommissioning (46% SLA, 39% archived/static, 15% migrated) is required.

deliverables.title: Interactive Web Evolution Diff & Timeline Explorer
deliverables.strongest_counterevidence: Web archive user studies indicate most users perform targeted navigational/link-rot lookups rather than open-ended museum browsing, and curating accurate interactive comparisons is labor-intensive.
deliverables.closest_existing_alternative: Wayback Machine Changes + Web Design Museum + Oldweb.today

deliverables.title: Retired-Runtime Scholarly & Educational Reading Room
deliverables.strongest_counterevidence: Target demand is a narrow academic niche, Ruffle/CheerpJ already cover many single-file artifacts, and complex works still require substantial archivist configuration effort as shown in EaaSI Case Study #1.
deliverables.closest_existing_alternative: EaaSI (Software Preservation Network), Internet Archive Emularity/Ruffle, Flashpoint Archive

deliverables.title: Provenance-Layered Digital Time Capsule & Community Exhibition
deliverables.strongest_counterevidence: High legal/ethical risk (privacy, GDPR right to be forgotten, community consent), weak Kiroween Resurrection theme anchor unless tied to a retired technology, and Conifer's June 2026 shutdown shows hosted community preservation struggles to sustain itself.
deliverables.closest_existing_alternative: Mukurtu CMS, Arquivo.pt Online Exhibitions, Internet Archive Collections
